nodes.name: Route by Work Type
nodes.notes: Routes each item to one of 3 lanes: sync, async + fallback. Watch out: Unmatched items go to the fallback output; without one they are silently dropped.

nodes.notes: Upserts into Airtable's 'Payloads' table, matched on itemId — safe to re-run without creating duplicates. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. nodes.notes: Sends a Telegram message to the configured chat — the same bot can also receive replies, so this doubles as a two-way ops channel. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. nodes.name: Hold Unknown Types (DLQ)
nodes.notes: Creates a new record in Airtable's 'Payloads' table. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Airtable PAT. airtable.com/create/tokens → create a Personal Access Token.

nodes.name: Merge Routed Work
nodes.notes: Rejoins 3 branches into one stream (mode: append) so downstream logic runs once. Watch out: Waits for every configured input. If one branch never produces items, add 'Always Output Data' upstream so this doesn't stall.

nodes.name: Guard Non-Empty source
nodes.notes: Drops items that fail the condition; only qualifying items continue (no false branch).

# Automate a routine task: Airtable & Telegram

**Pattern:** Workflow Automation · **Level:** Intermediate · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers helpers work end to end across Airtable, Telegram and Slack.

It moves through 15 working steps plus a 2-node error rail, in this order:

1. Hourly Schedule
2. Keep Valid Payloads
3. Route by Work Type
4. Process 'sync' → Airtable
5. Fast-Track 'async' + Alert
6. Hold Unknown Types (DLQ)
7. Merge Routed Work
8. Guard Non-Empty source
9. Stamp Processing Time
10. Cap Batch Volume
11. Save Execution Metadata
12. Tag Pipeline Metadata
13. Summarize Run Stats
14. Append Audit Row (Airtable)
15. Send Summary to Telegram

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing helpers work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Hourly Schedule → Keep Valid Payloads → Route by Work Type → Process 'sync' → Airtable → Fast-Track 'async' + Alert → Hold Unknown Types (DLQ) → Merge Routed Work → Guard Non-Empty source → Stamp Processing Time → Cap Batch Volume → Save Execution Metadata → Tag Pipeline Metadata → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Airtable) → Send Summary to Telegram → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Airtable and Telegram aligned by hand for helpers
- Helpers work where "Keep Valid Payloads" is still a manual step before Airtable
- Helpers work that only reaches Airtable on a schedule, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Airtable and Telegram in step for helpers, without anyone re-typing a row
- A failed Airtable or Telegram call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 17 nodes in this helpers build
- Branches rejoin before Airtable, so a helpers run reports once rather than 17 times
- Every helpers run leaves an audit row behind, alongside Airtable
- Fans the same result out to Slack in the same run, for helpers

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Airtable PAT; Slack OAuth2; Telegram bot token.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Unrecognized work types are parked in a dead-letter lane instead of erroring the whole run or silently dropping the item — new event kinds will show up eventually, and this is where you'd notice one without losing it. One kind is deliberately routed through a sub-workflow to show how heavier per-type logic can be extracted without touching this router at all.

## Practice exercises

You've got the basics covered — push further:

1. Send a work-type value that matches no switch rule and confirm it lands in the dead-letter branch.
2. Add a new work type and its own handling branch.
3. Replace the direct-write branch with a sub-workflow call, matching the pattern already used for the first kind.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Airtable PAT**
airtable.com/create/tokens → create a Personal Access Token.
_Gotcha:_ Scope the token to the specific base, and grant `data.records:write`. Field names are case-sensitive.

**Telegram bot token**
Message @BotFather on Telegram → /newbot → copy the token.
_Gotcha:_ Get your chat ID by messaging the bot then opening api.telegram.org/bot<TOKEN>/getUpdates.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your helpers process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Airtable: scope the PAT to this one base and to `data.records:write`; a token scoped to the workspace can rewrite every base.
- Telegram: the bot token is a bearer credential — rotate it if it ever appears in an execution log.
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole helpers payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.
